h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When edge 3 already convolves the input into node3, a second parallel conv into node3 is partly redundant.
Pairing an identity shortcut with a conv path through node1 creates a residual block that trains better.
Stacking two 3x3 convs along 0->1->2 builds a deep, large-receptive-field chain that weaker predecessors cannot provide.
A skip from node1 forwards the blurred pooled map unprocessed into the output sum, contaminating it.
Pooling at the end of a path that just paid for a conv discards the spatial detail that conv computed.
With the deep route via node2 cut, the direct edge becomes a main carrier of processing into node3, so a conv there matters more.
When node1's route is degraded by pooling, a direct conv into node2 supplies the sharp processed features the cell otherwise lacks.
If edge 5 is already cut, removing edge 4 leaves node3 fed only by edge 3, collapsing the cell to a near-trivial network.
When edge 4 already delivers convolved detail to node3, pooling on edge 5 costs less because the cell keeps a strong processed route.
With edge 2 cut, edge 1 is node2's sole input, so making it a conv determines whether the 0->2->3 route carries processed features at all.
